title: LangTime: A Language-Guided Unified Model for Time Series Forecasting with Proximal Policy Optimization
methods: Cross-domain LLM time-series model with TimePPO fine-tuning.
findings: TimePPO reward is a tanh-bounded weighted sum of RMSE, MAE and KL dimensions minus a beta MSE penalty against the reference policy, plus an alignment-tax prediction loss.
limitations: General forecasting benchmarks, not medical. Gains over SFT are small on several datasets.
notes: Local PDF 2503.08271v2 inspected.

title: Time Series Forecasting via Reasoning: A Slow-Thinking Approach with Reinforcement Fine-Tuned LLMs

locators.C005: p. 5, structural similarity reward; p. 9 MSE as primary accuracy reward

methods: SFT warmup on synthetic CoT then GRIP, a non-uniform-sampling variant of GRPO.
findings: Reward combines point accuracy with seasonal, trend and extrema-matching terms. Authors later adopt MSE as the primary accuracy reward after comparing MAE, DTW and MAPE.
limitations: CIKM 2026 version inspected as arXiv v4. Not a clinical dataset. Synthetic CoT is generated by another LLM.
notes: Local PDF 2506.10630v4.

title: Reasoning on Time-Series for Financial Technical Analysis

locators.C003: p. 4, Eq. 4 inverse MSE reward; ICLR 2026

methods: Time-GRPO on verbal technical-analysis traces, then conditional time-series backbone.
findings: Reward is format compliance plus inverse MSE of the verbal forecast. Cold start, rejection sampling at the 10th percentile MSE, then GRPO.
limitations: Stock data only. Inverse MSE is unstable when error approaches zero.
notes: Local PDF 2511.08616v2, published as ICLR 2026 conference paper per PDF header.

title: TimeSRL: Generalizable Time-Series Behavioral Modeling via Semantic RL-Tuned LLMs
methods: Semantic bottleneck: raw behavioral series to language summary to PHQ-4 score, jointly optimized by GRPO.
findings: Invalid format receives zero reward. Valid scores use exp(-(p-y)^2/(2 sigma^2)). Outcome reward trains the intermediate summary without gold annotations.
limitations: Mental-health passive sensing, not influenza deterioration. Preprint. Trained on four H100s.
notes: Local PDF 2605.21295v1. Closest medical behavioral time-series RL post-training.

title: REATS: LLM Reasoning-based Ensemble Learning for Adaptive Time Series Forecasting
methods: 1.7B LLM routes ensemble weights with SFT then GRPO.
findings: Naive negative MSE gap collapses GRPO advantages. Reciprocal map 1/(1+k delta) with k=20, lambda (0.8, 0, 0.2), format penalty -0.5.
limitations: General univariate benchmarks, not medical. Oracle weights use training-set ground truth.
notes: Local PDF 2608.10149v1.

title: TimeRFT: Stimulating Generalizable Time Series Forecasting for TSFMs via Reinforcement Finetuning

locators.C007: p. 7, single 96GB GPU, Moirai-MoE, Toto, Chronos-2

methods: GRPO-style reinforcement fine-tuning of TSFMs with step-wise accuracy, variability and frequency rewards.
findings: Accuracy-only rewards encourage oversmoothed forecasts. Ground-truth is added to the reward group and piecewise-shaped. Weights lambda_acc=0.9, lambda_var=0.1, lambda_syn=0.01.
limitations: Not a medical cohort. Conference template still contains placeholder venue text, so peer-review status is not established from the PDF.
notes: Downloaded PDF inspected 2026-09-23.

title: Rethinking Post-Training Recipes for Multimodal Time-Series Forecasting

locators.C007: p. 8, dual A100; Gemma-3-4B revises TimesFM-2.5

methods: SFT plus RLVR where the LLM revises, preserves or ignores a TSFM prior.
findings: Exponential MAE reward has mean within-group standard deviation 0.0171 and 27.97% near-zero-variance groups. Improvement-ratio reward raises that to 0.0719 and 4.66%.
limitations: Multimodal benchmark, not clinical deterioration. SFT accounts for most of the gain; RL adds a smaller increment.
notes: Downloaded PDF inspected. Google Research / Georgia Tech preprint.

title: medR: Reward Engineering for Clinical Offline Reinforcement Learning via Tri-Drive Potential Functions

locators.C010: Appendix E.3-E.4; Table 2 claim of WIS gains

methods: LLM generates potential-based rewards; offline fitness selects among candidates.
findings: R = gamma Phi(s',t') - Phi(s,t) - lambda C(a). Phi multiplies strategic decay, feature survival score and staleness weight. Action cost breaks policy invariance and matches a CMDP Lagrangian.
limitations: Treatment policy, not forecast loss. WIS is retrospective. LLM-written reward code needs clinician audit. Author list not re-extracted in this pass; identity verified against local full text and prior audit.
notes: Full text previously downloaded as 2602.03305; formula sections re-read 2026-09-23.

title: Advancing Safe Mechanical Ventilation Using Offline RL With Hybrid Actions and Clinically Aligned Rewards
methods: Hybrid-action offline RL with ventilator-free-day reward and physiological range terms.
findings: Authors reject mortality as the sole endpoint because it is confounded. VFD combines survival and liberation from ventilation. Unseen clinician actions are removed from the discrete action space.
limitations: Ventilation policy, not influenza forecasting. Dataset and clinical co-design details are stronger than external outcome evidence.
notes: Downloaded PDF inspected.

title: From Robotics to Sepsis Treatment: Offline RL via Geometric Pessimism
methods: kNN distance in state-action embedding becomes a precomputed reward penalty inside IQL.
findings: r_geo = r - lambda_adapt * max(0, U). On MIMIC-III sepsis, author reports 86.4% terminal clinician agreement versus 75% for IQL, and training on a laptop GPU.
limitations: Single-author preprint. Agreement with clinicians is not patient benefit. Sepsis cohort is not influenza.
notes: Downloaded PDF inspected.

title: Offline Guarded Safe Reinforcement Learning for Medical Treatment Optimization Strategies

locators.C010: p. 1, 78% mortality-estimate reduction is an offline estimate

methods: Model-based offline RL with an OOD guardian on state-action regions plus a physiological safety cost.
findings: CQL-style action penalties do not stop later states from leaving the data support. Safety cost is separate from the reward.
limitations: Mortality and reward gains are offline estimates on MIMIC-III sepsis, not prospective outcomes.
notes: Abstract and introduction inspected; later pages had extraction limits.

title: Guardian-regularized Safe Offline Reinforcement Learning for Smart Weaning of Mechanical Circulatory Devices
methods: CORMPO: clinical reward shaping plus density penalty, evaluated in a transformer digital twin.
findings: Reward is physiological score minus action-change penalty plus weaning score. Real patient data are not public.
limitations: ML4H 2025 paper. Device weaning, not influenza. Digital-twin evaluation can share model error with training.
notes: PDF header states ML4H 2025 proceedings.

title: Reinforcement Learning in Dynamic Treatment Regimes Needs Critical Reexamination
methods: Position paper with a large sepsis offline-RL evaluation case study.
findings: RL rankings change with the metric and the MDP formulation. In some settings RL does not beat naive or supervised baselines.
limitations: Abstract-only in this pass. Does not itself propose a reward formula.
notes: Abstract retrieved from arXiv API before rate limiting.

title: MIRA: Medical Time Series Foundation Model for Real-World Health Data

locators.C001: prior full-text audit pp. 1-4; arXiv API title confirmation 2026-09-23

methods: Continuous-time medical time-series foundation model.
findings: Pretraining and forecasting objective. No RL post-training described in the inspected materials.
limitations: Model size and fine-tuning memory were not established in the prior audit.
notes: Identity confirmed by arXiv API. Full text was read in the 2026-09-22 audit, not re-read page by page today.

title: Fine-Tuning Foundation Models with Federated Learning for Privacy Preserving Medical Time Series Forecasting

locators.C001: prior audit pp. 4-7; arXiv API confirmation

methods: Federated and local fine-tuning of an approximately 8M Chronos model on ECG/ICG.
findings: Post-training is supervised forecasting loss, not a clinical reward.
limitations: Not influenza. Local tuning can beat federated averaging under non-IID splits.
notes: Full text inspected in prior audit; identity reconfirmed by API.

title: Repurposing Foundation Model for Generalizable Medical Time Series Classification
methods: FORMED adapts a generic time-series backbone with channel embeddings, label queries and a shared decoder.
findings: Lightweight supervised adaptation, not RL.
limitations: Abstract-only this pass. Classification, not deterioration forecasting.
notes: PDF downloaded but formula not required for the claim.

title: MOTOR: A Time-To-Event Foundation Model For Structured Medical Records
methods: Self-supervised time-to-event pretraining on structured records.
findings: Up to 55 million patients and 9 billion events. Objective is censored time-to-event likelihood, not RL.
limitations: Abstract-page access only in this pass.
notes: Verified via arXiv HTML abstract.

title: Learning the natural history of human disease with generative transformers

locators.C001: PubMed abstract PMID 40963019, as retrieved by literature agent

methods: Delphi-2M modified GPT for competing disease rates and timings.
findings: Trained on 0.4 million UK Biobank participants and externally evaluated on 1.9 million Danish records without parameter updates, per retrieved abstract.
limitations: Abstract-level. Not re-fetched from the publisher page in this session. Author list abbreviated because the agent summary did not preserve the full byline.
notes: PMID 40963019. Use as context for event-time generative models, not as an RL paper.

title: Zero shot health trajectory prediction using transformer
methods: ETHOS tokenizes patient timelines and predicts next events zero-shot.
findings: Authors argue labeled fine-tuning is unnecessary for the reported trajectory tasks.
limitations: Abstract-level. Cohort details not re-verified from the PDF.
notes: Included to show that medical trajectory FMs often stop at generative pretraining.

title: Reinforcement Learning over Patient Trajectories for Clinical Reasoning in EHR Foundation Models
methods: Treats an EHR foundation model as a generative policy and RL-fine-tunes trajectory continuation.
findings: Reward is described as time-aware and rollout-sensitive to handle finite rollouts and temporally inconclusive outcomes. Dataset is not named on the abstract page.
limitations: Abstract-only. Formula, cohort and model size were not on the inspected page. Very recent preprint.
notes: Most direct EHR-FM RL post-training candidate found. Do not cite a formula.

title: QoQ-Med: Building Multimodal Clinical Foundation Models with Domain-Aware GRPO Training
methods: Instruction tuning then domain-aware GRPO on images, ECG and text.
findings: After per-question normalization, advantages are scaled by domain and cluster temperatures so rarer or harder groups are not drowned out.
limitations: Diagnostic multimodal tasks, not deterioration forecasting. HTML extract, not the publisher PDF.
notes: ar5iv HTML inspected after arXiv API rate limit.

title: Ground-Truth Neighborhood Regularization for Reinforcement Learning Post-Training of Time Series Foundation Models
methods: GTN-R plug-in regularizer for RL post-training of forecasting models.
findings: Authors name suboptimal collapse when RL moves probability mass away from the ground truth because high-quality trajectories are rarely sampled.
limitations: Abstract-only. No equation inspected. Not medical.
notes: Verified on arXiv abstract page.

title: Time Series Reasoning via Process-Verifiable Thinking Data Synthesis and Scheduling for Tailored LLM Reasoning
methods: Synthetic process-checkable traces, difficulty scheduling, two-stage RL fine-tuning.
findings: Uses fine-grained multi-objective rewards from process-level labels.
limitations: Abstract-only. Formula not inspected. Not medical.
notes: Verified on arXiv abstract page.

title: TimeHF: Billion-Scale Time Series Models Guided by Human Feedback
methods: 6B industrial forecasting model with a human-feedback stage.
findings: Names a human feedback mechanism called time-series policy optimization. Does not define the reward on the abstract page.
limitations: Industrial claim of +33.21% is author-reported and not independently inspected. Not medical.
notes: Retained only as evidence that human-feedback post-training exists, not as a formula source.

title: SurvivEHR: a competing risks, time-to-event foundation model for multiple long-term conditions
methods: Competing-risk pretraining then prognosis fine-tuning.
findings: 23 million UK primary-care patients. Objective is time-to-event, not RL.
limitations: Abstract-level. Full author list not retained in the agent extract, so not cited for author-specific claims.
notes: Used only for the existence of competing-risk EHR foundation-model post-training.

title: A generalist medical language model for disease diagnosis assistance
methods: MedFound: medical pretraining, self-bootstrapped chain-of-thought fine-tuning, unified preference alignment.
findings: Preference alignment is used, but the abstract does not name DPO or RLHF or give a reward formula. 176B parameters.
limitations: Text diagnosis model, not a time-series forecaster. Abstract-level.
notes: Context only. Not a transferable time-series reward.

title: Reinforcement learning for intensive care medicine: actionable clinical insights from novel approaches to reward shaping and off-policy model evaluation

locators.C008: PubMed 38526681 abstract, gas-exchange interim rewards and mortality terminal rewards

methods: Dueling DDQN for PEEP and FiO2, with policy restriction and cross off-policy evaluation.
findings: Interim reward is gas exchange; terminal reward is mortality and state duration. The abstract states that 44% of policies that looked good failed when interim versus terminal weighting changed.
limitations: Abstract-only. COVID-19 ventilation, not influenza deterioration prediction. Author byline not extracted from XML in this pass.
notes: Article DOI verified from PubmedData ArticleIdList, not reference list.

title: Reinforcement learning for treatment decision-making in sepsis: a scoping review
methods: Scoping review of 72 retrospective sepsis RL studies.
findings: 58 of 72 used MIMIC. Reward definitions vary widely. Claimed outperformance of clinicians is not reliably evaluable.
limitations: Abstract of a review, not a new reward formula. Full author list not extracted.
notes: Used as coverage and evaluation-limitation evidence.

title: Optimal Vasopressin Initiation in Septic Shock: The OVISS Reinforcement Learning Study
methods: Offline RL initiation rule for vasopressin, evaluated with weighted importance sampling and inverse-probability-weighted regression.
findings: Derived on 3,608 patients and evaluated on internal plus 10,217 external patients. Primary endpoint is in-hospital mortality. Reward equation is not in the abstract.
limitations: Abstract truncated. Observational EHR. Not a forecast post-training paper.
notes: Retained as the strongest multi-hospital clinical RL evaluation found, not as a formula source.
